newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-TOUR GAMES THREATENED BY ENGLISH POWER STRUGGLE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TOUR GAMES THREATENED BY ENGLISH POWER STRUGGLE.

text.p: Jonah Lomu could find himself playing against third division English opposition next month in the latest twist to the long-running dispute between the top clubs and the Rugby Football Union (RFU).

The clubs announced on Thursday they would release players for international duty and backed down on threats to split from the RFU, but have said they will block the release of players for divisional matches against touring teams.

The New Zealand Barbarians, whose squad includes Lomu and the bulk of the current All Black team, Queensland, the Junior Springboks and Argentina could all be affected over the next two months if no solution is found.
As it stands the touring sides will not face players from the top two leagues in England outside test matches, although pressure might be put on the players to ignore the clubs' directive.

"We will select our first-choice teams for these matches and leave it up to the players to decide," said RFU secretary Tony Hallett. "If they decline our invitations, we will re-select until we put 15 players on the pitch."

The RFU and the clubs are still divided over broadcasting revenue and the control of club competitions, but England coach Jack Rowell can at least now select a full-strength team against Italy on November 23.
Rowell indicated the identity of England's new captain would be made public before the end of the month.
